title: CO-DESIGNING YITPI YARTAPUULTIKU
venue: Allan Scott Auditorium H2-16, Fenn Place, Adelaide University, ADL CBD
blurb:
YITPI YARTAPUULTIKU - Soul of Port Adelaide: The Story Behind an Award-Winning Place

Discover the remarkable story behind YITPI YARTAPUULTIKU - Soul of Port Adelaide, a multi-award-winning public realm project that has transformed the heart of Port Adelaide. Join Architect Ashley Halliday and Landscape Architect Warwick Keates as they take the audience behind the scenes of the project's conception, design development, and delivery.

This engaging presentation explores how architecture, landscape architecture, planning, culture, history, and community aspirations were woven together to create a place of lasting significance. Through insights into the co-design process, working with cultural knowledge, key challenges, and moments of innovation, Ashley and Warwick reveal the thinking that shaped a project now recognised for its design excellence and contribution to public life.

Whether you are a design professional, student, or community member, this presentation offers a unique opportunity to understand how thoughtful, place-based design can celebrate identity, strengthen connection, and leave a lasting legacy for future generations.

A free event, bookings essential. Presented by the School of Architecture and Built Environment, Adelaide University.
contributors: Ashley Halliday (Ashley Halliday Architects); Warwick Keates (WAX Design)

title: JON GOULDER x AGSA
blurb: Join Rebecca Evans, Curator of Decorative Arts and Design for a special Adelaide Design Week Tuesday Talk with South Australian craftsperson and designer, Jon Goulder. Jon Goulder is a fourth-generation furniture designer and maker. Goulder completed his apprenticeship in furniture making and upholstery with his family’s business E W Goulder and Sons, between 1988-1992. In 1996 he moved to Canberra to study furniture design and fine woodworking at Canberra School of Art under the direction of the late George Ingham. After leaving Canberra School of Art he established his design consultancy – ’Jon Goulder Designer Maker’. Goulder is both a designer and a talented furniture maker- a rarity in the Australian and international design community. Between 2013-2018 he was Creative Director (Furniture) Jam Factory Adelaide, he was previously a Senior Designer with Snohetta Architects Australasia. He currently runs his own studio space in the southern suburbs of Adelaide.
contributors: Jon Goulder; Rebecca Evans

contributors: GGA exhibition design team + AGSA curatorial team

venue: Immersive Art and Installation, 63 Light Sq, CBD, ADL

title: THE AUSTRALIAN (DESIGN) DREAM
contributors: Kim Bridgland (Studio All Days); Alana Hanton (design by WBL); Kate Bowen (Fabrikate); Max Cairns (Jardan); Moderated by Bronwyn Marshall

title: THE FRINGE CONDITION : EXTREME DESIGN
blurb: What does it mean to design for life at the fringe of human existence? The Fringe Condition is an exhibition and panel discussion exploring one of the most radical design briefs of our time, building for human life on the Moon, and what that means for communities here on Earth.
contributors: Amit Srivastava; Albert Rajkumar; Meriem Allani; Souktik Bhattacherjee; Monika Stankiewicz; Kato Claeys; Kara Simpson

title: UNBUILT : MEET THE DESIGNERS
blurb: > UNBUILT — Obstacles > Sunday 18 October 10am-11am > PARABOLICA × SSdH × LIAN × Office Alex Nicholls > Emerging practice and the forces that prevent architecture from making the transition from idea to building. > > UNBUILT — Remnants > Sunday 18 October 11am-12pm > OFFICE × A22a × Martina Beka > What remains after demolition, and how materials can be recovered, reinterpreted and given another use. > > UNBUILT — Speculation > Sunday 18 October 1pm-2pm > Trower Falvo × 877c × Moraene × Office Ren > Architecture untethered from the certainty of construction: propositions, competitions, provocations and ideas pursued for their own value. > > UNBUILT — Meanwhile > Sunday 18 October 2pm-3pm > Found Artefact Curators × Craft Architecture × Tusk > Temporary occupation, interim use and what buildings can become in the space between one permanent condition and another.
contributors: PARABOLICA × SSdH × LIAN × Office Alex Nicholls; OFFICE × A22a × Martina Beka; Trower Falvo × 877c × Moraene × Office Ren; Found Artefact Curators × Craft Architecture × Tusk

venue: The Forum, Jeffrey Smart, ADL CBD

venue: The Forum, Jeffrey Smart, ADL CBD

title: EVERY*BIKE TOUR
blurb: The Every*bike Tour is a casual cycling tour connecting ADW exhibitions, events, designers, studios, curators, makers, workshops, artists, galleries, places and people together by bike. Each stop along the way is a chance to meet, learn and discover an exciting and energised creative Adelaide! BYO Bike :)
contributors: Tim Grisbrook / MOOD

title: INSIDE INNOVATION : INSIDE QANTAS TOUR
blurb: Interior designers are invited to join us for a walk-through of Qantas’ newly opened Product Innovation Centre in Adelaide. The tour will be led by Concept CI, the interior designer behind the space, together with Klaro Industrial Design, who supplied the furniture. Together, they’ll take guests through key elements of the interior, design decisions and furniture solutions in an informal, conversational format.
contributors: Concept CI; Klaro Industrial Design; Qantas

title: LISTENING WITH ARCHITECTURE
venue: MEET: Jewels of Thought Records, Ebenezer Place CBD, ADL
blurb: What kinds of acoustic spaces does the architecture of our city offer us? How might these spaces ground us. How might they serve to expand our sense of self? Join artist and educator Tom Borgas on a guided listening experience of some of his favourite east-end pockets of sonic intensity.
contributors: Tom Borgas

title: MODERNIST ADELAIDE WALKING TOUR
venue: MEET: Faraway House, 21 Franklin Street, CBD, ADL
blurb: Adelaide's mid-century boom produced a revolution of modernist architecture most locals walk past without a glance. Stuart Symons' award-winning tours have drawn international acclaim and a devoted cult following, tracing how global design ideas took flight in Adelaide during the 1950s–70s. 'Jewel-like' – Kevin McCloud, Grand Designs
contributors: Stuart Symons

title: TORRENS RIVER CITY WALK
venue: MEET: Sir Douglas Nicholls Bridge, CBD ADL
blurb: Walk the River Torrens like never before. Using an interactive mobile map, this guided walk reveals 150 years of urban design evolution. View archival photos of exact locations and see how GeoAI analyzed Adelaide's heritage landscape to track changes in infrastructure, vegetation, and public life.
contributors: Mohamad Waheed Fareed Abdelfattah

title: MAKE AN IMPRESSION : ARLON HALL / BILLIE JUSTICE THOMSON (all ages)
blurb: South Australian artists Arlon Hall and Billie Justice Thomson invite you to slow down and lose yourself inside a painting. Thomson's vibrant compositions draw on everyday objects, Australian imagery and familiar food and drink, evoking a quiet sense of nostalgia. Hall works across painting, drawing and sculpture, exploring the interplay of line, colour and form through moments of overlap and tension. Inspired by Monet to Matisse: Defying Tradition this Studio invites hands-on exploration of light, colour, line and shape to create your own abstract coloured, layered line drawing.
contributors: Arlon Hall and Billie Justice Thomson

title: THE DIGITAL PAUSE - Collage Evening
venue: Being Studio, 27 Halifax St, CBD, ADL
blurb: Together with Klaro, we’re hosting an analogue collage night, The Digital Pause! Join us for a relaxed evening to unplug, unwind, and create your own vision board for the design practice you want to manifest. We’ll have magazines, fabric offcuts and catalogues on hand, plus some refreshments.
contributors: Being Studio & Klaro Industrial Design

title: THREADING STORIES
blurb: Threading Stories is a community quilting workshop grounded in care, creativity and storytelling. This workshop allows participants to sew or embellish a shared quilt. Open to everyone from beginner to advanced sewers and storytellers, to printmakers, painters and mixed media creatives.
contributors: Stella Martino

title: WAX CARVING : RING MAKING
venue: Min Jewellery, g14 33 Pirie St, CBD, ADL
blurb: Wax carving ring making work shop. Work with wax and tools to design and shape your unique ring. Your wax design will be professionally cast, sanded, and finished by the instructor. In approximately two weeks, your completed sterling silver ring will be ready for you to collect
